plate_findings.evidence: Caption identifies retiform purpura; branching violaceous-black lesions are visible.
Caption identifies advanced-stage necrotic ulcers in a classical reticulated format.
Large dark necrotic eschar is visibly present within the ulcers.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of lower limbs showing retiform purpura and extensive advanced necrotic ulceration with black eschar, explicitly captioned as classical calciphylaxis. [raw subtype: classical calciphylaxis] B: Close-up clinical photograph showing a necrotic ulcer with dark eschar, explicitly attributed by the caption to calciphylaxis. [raw subtype: classical calciphylaxis]

panels.rationale: The caption directly attributes the histopathology to a calciphylaxis lesion and specifies vessel-wall calcium deposition and intimal proliferation, with associated subcutaneous fat necrosis. The single H&E panel is therefore a qualifying real-patient histopathology image.
panels.attribution_text: Lacerda et al. Livedoid vasculopathy, calciphylaxis, and Martorell's hypertensive ulcer: update on ischemic ulcers due to impaired microcirculation of the lower limbs.. panels.figure_caption: Histopathology of calciphylaxis lesion. Necrosis of subcutaneous fat, with significant calcium deposition on the vessel wall and intima proliferation (Hematoxylin & eosin, ×400).
in_text_mentions: taneous tissue, outside necrotic areas. The main histopathological findings are calcification of small vessels, intimal hyperplasia, and thrombotic occlusion of vessels in the dermis and subcutaneous tissue. Inflammatory infiltration is frequently observed (Fig. 5). Specific stains to demonstrate the presence of calcium in the tissue, such as von Kossa staining, are important to confirm the diagnosis.27, 40Fig. 5Histopathology of calciphylaxis lesion. panels.rationale: Human skin-biopsy histology directly demonstrates ulceration, necrosis, marked vascular calcification, and thrombi in small and intermediate subcutaneous vessels, consistent with calciphylaxis.

panels.figure_caption: Case 7 - skin biopsy Ulceration of the epidermis with severe acute inflammation and necrosis with marked calcification and thrombi within the small and intermediate vessels of the subcutaneous tissue in keeping with Calciphylaxis
in_text_mentions: The patient's lab investigations are illustrated in Table 1. A wound swab of the ulcer grew Pseudomonas and E. Coli. The patient was subsequently treated with piperacillin/tazobactam. X-rays were arranged for suspected calciphylaxis (Figure 12) and along with a skin biopsy (Figure 13).
